question: Does a monthly Labour Force Survey result describe what respondents did throughout the whole month?

Employment refers to the number of people who are currently working for pay, whether they are employed full-time or part-time. Hours worked refers to the total number of hours worked by all employed persons during the reference week. This includes both paid and unpaid hours. Labour force participation rate refers to the percentage of the population that is currently either employed or unemployed, but actively looking for work. This includes both employed persons and unemployed persons. What is the difference between unemployment and underemployment? This includes both discouraged workers who have given up looking for work and people who are not currently in the labour force.
